Empty project. I need to build a complete playable game: RuneScape-like (OSRS style: click-to-move, skills, skilling, combat, inventory, quests, leveling) set in GTA V's Los Santos setting (gangs, heists, cars, wanted level, etc.).

Let me plan a tech stack. Pure HTML/CSS/JS with canvas rendering — no build step needed. Use a 2D tile-based top-down world with OSRS-style click movement and skills, themed as Los Santos: skills like Driving, Shooting, Stealth, Hacking, Strength, Stamina, Charisma, Cooking (food trucks), Mechanics, Chemistry (drug cooking? keep it tasteful), Fishing (pier), Mining? Let me map GTA-flavored skills:

RuneScape skills → GTA skills:
- Attack/Strength/Defence → Firepower? Let's use: Shooting, Strength, Stamina (defence)
- Hitpoints → Health
- Prayer → Reputation? 
- Magic → Hacking
- Ranged → Driving (drive-by)
- Slayer → Assassination/Contracts
- Fishing → Fishing (Vespucci pier) — keep for flavor
- Cooking → Cooking (food trucks)
- Mining/Smithing → Mechanic/Crafting (weapon mods)
- Woodcutting/Fletching → ? 
- Thieving → Stealing (pickpocket, car theft)
- Agility → Parkour
- Herblore → Chemistry (makes "med kits"?)
- Farming → dealing? Hmm.

Make 10 skills manageable: Shooting, Strength, Stamina, Driving, Hacking, Stealing, Parkour, Cooking, Fishing, Mechanics. Plus Health level. Maybe keep it to 8-10.

Gameplay loop: top-down 2D Los Santos map (tile-based). Click to move (click-to-walk with pathfinding like OSRS on grid). NPCs to talk to, shops, jobs, combat with gangs, wanted level, cars (drive them with WASD), heist quest. XP on actions like in RuneScape: chop tree → mining rock; here: pickpocket pedestrians, steal cars, shoot gangsters, hack ATMs, fish at pier, cook at food truck, repair cars.

I need a complete, polished, playable game. This is a big build. Let me design carefully but implement in a single-page app with modular JS files (no build step), canvas-based, with a HUD in DOM.

Key features:
1. Tile world ~120x90 tiles, with districts: Downtown (skyscrapers), Vinewood Hills, Grove Street (gang), Vespucci Beach (pier/fishing), Industrial (garage), Sandy Shores desert maybe. Buildings as blocked tiles. Roads network. Map authored procedurally + fixed landmarks for performance and coherence.
2. Click-to-move pathfinding (A* on grid) with OSRS-style click markers, minimap.
3. Player sprite drawn procedurally (stick-ish but nice: top-down character with shadow, directional facing, walk animation).
4. Skills panel with levels, XP bars, XP drops, level-up jingle via WebAudio.
5. Inventory 28 slots, items with icons drawn via emoji or canvas icons. Use emoji for items? Could be visually decent with color-coded tiles. Better draw simple pixel icons with canvas? Might be a lot. Emoji is fast and readable (🔫, 🍔, 🐟, 💊, 🔧, 📱, 💎, 🚗 key). I'll use emoji with styling.
6. Combat: click NPC to attack; auto-attack with cooldown, damage rolls based on level; NPCs hit back; health regen; death respawn at hospital with item loss? Keep death penalty mild.
7. Cars: click car to enter, then WASD/arrow driving with physics-ish car movement, hitting pedestrians/gangsters gives XP and wanted level. Exit with E. Maybe driving collisions block movement.
8. Wanted level stars, police spawn when wanted; cops chase/shoot; bribe with cash at pay 'n' spray to clear.
9. Shops: Ammu-Nation (buy guns/ammo/armor), 24/7 store (food), mechanic (repair), pay'n'spray.
10. Quests / jobs: 
   - Main "story" with steps: talk to Lamar at Grove Street → steal a car → deliver to garage → shoot Ballas → hack ATM → heist finale at bank. Simple dialogue panel.
   - Repeatable jobs: pizza delivery? taxi? Keep a "contracts" board? Maybe simpler: quest chain + repeatable side activities (steal cars, rob stores, fish, cook, hack ATMs).
11. Feeding / hunger? Not needed.
12. Save/load to localStorage.
13. Mobile touch support: on-screen joystick? Since click-to-move, touch tap works for movement; add action buttons (attack nearest, enter/exit car, inventory). Ensure responsive.
14. Audio: WebAudio synth for gunshots, pickups, level up, ambient music maybe simple. Keep light.
15. Nice UI: OSRS-ish ornate panels but GTA-ish neon. Use dark UI with gold/green accents, "LS" branding. Use Google font? No network maybe. Use system fonts with fallback; could use CSS fonts like 'Georgia' for fantasy, but GTA uses Pricedown. Use bold sans with skew for logo. Avoid external assets.
16. Title screen with instructions, start/continue.
17. Screenshots with playwright-cli at 1280x800.

Also check if there's a default server script? The start.sh points to runtime dir which likely doesn't exist locally. I'll create my own static server for testing (python3 -m http.server on port 3002) OR use playwright with file://? Better use server at 3002 per Agents.md.

# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).

No existing game. Let's build from scratch. Plan the architecture.

I'll make a 2D top-down game in HTML5 canvas with modular JS files loaded as ES modules. Serve with python http.server on port 3002 via tmux.

Game design: "LOS SANTOS: STREETS" — an OSRS-inspired MMORPG-style game set in GTA V's Los Santos.

Core experience:
- Title screen with logo & continue.
- World map top-down, ~110 x 80 tiles, 32px tiles.
- Camera follows player.
- Click to move with A* pathfinding, click markers.
- NPCs with names/dialogue.
- Skills: 10 skills + Health. XP curve OSRS-like (level 99). To make progress reasonably fast, use OSRS XP table but multiply XP gains, or use simplified xp = level^3? RuneScape XP table has level 99 at 13,034,431. Too slow for a demo. Use "fast" curve: xpToLevel(l) = sum for 1..l. Maybe level 30-40 reachable in session. Make level 99 possible but not necessary. I'll use formula xp = 100 * (level-1)^2.5? Hmm, make capped at 50? Better to show 99 as max with a steeper but grindable curve. xp for level L = floor(75*(L-1)^2.2)? Level 10 = 75*9^2.2≈75*132=9900; level 30 = 75*29^2.2≈75*1930=145k. Too slow. Use level cap 50 with xp = 60*(L-1)^2. Level 10=4860, 25=34,560, 50=144k. XP per action 20-100 → leveling to 20 in a session doable. Hmm, RuneScape style expects 99. I'll display level/99 but use curve xp = 80*(L-1)^2; level 99 = 768k. At ~40 XP/action that's 19k actions — too slow but fine for a demo (people won't reach 99). Cap displayed 99. Actually let's make combat XP ~ 50-200 per kill, thieving 30 per steal. Level 20 needs 80*361=28,880 XP → 200 steals = long. Hmm. Let's tune: xp needed for level L = 50*(L-1)^2. Level 10:4050, 20:18,050, 30:42,050, 50:120,050, 99:480,200. Kills give 100-300. Fine.

Combat system:
- Attack target by clicking NPC (if weapon equipped / fists). Player auto-attacks every ~1.2s when in range, then NPC retaliates.
- Hit chance via level diff, damage random. XP to Shooting (ranged) or Strength (melee). Weapons: fists (melee), pistol, SMG, rifle, shotgun. Ammo counts.
- Health level = 10 + 5*level? Actually HP 10 at start, 100 max. Damage 2-8.
- NPCs: pedestrians (neutral, can rob), Ballas gangsters (hostile, attack on sight in Grove area), cops (spawn with wanted), shopkeepers (non-combat), quest givers, animals? 
- Wanted stars: crimes (attack peds, steal cars, kill) add heat; cops spawn; at 3+ stars more cops. Pay'n'Spray clears for $200. Death → hospital respawn, lose cash 10%.

Movement/economy:
- Pickpocket pedestrian: click "Rob" action or click ped with Stealing active? Use context: click ped → if unarmed intimidation? Simpler: right-click? Mobile issues. Use a "target" panel when clicking NPC with buttons: Talk / Attack / Pickpocket. That's nice and explicit like OSRS but easier on mobile. However auto attack click is core. I'll do: clicking NPC opens small context menu near cursor with options based on NPC type. That's both desktop/mobile friendly. Also keyboard shortcuts? Keep context menu.
- Clicking ground moves. Clicking car: context "Enter car" / "Steal" (if locked, need Stealing level).
- Clicking objects: trees? For fishing, click pier water spots; cooking at food truck; hacking at ATM; mining? For mechanic skill, click broken-down cars scattered; repairing gives XP + cash. Parkour: climb rooftop markers? Do simple "parkour spots" (ledges) that give XP + cash and teleport you over a wall. Might skip teleports; parkour checkpoints give XP.

- Shops: Ammu-Nation buy pistol/ammo/armor; Clothing? 24/7 buy snacks (heal); Pay'n'Spray clear wanted & repair; Garage for quest deliveries, mechanic repair; Bank ATM hack for cash (needs hacking level, gives money & wanted). 
- Fishing at pier: click fishing spot, catches fish with Cooking XP? Fishing XP, raw fish cooked at food truck for Cooking XP, eat for HP.
- Stealing cars: enter unowned car (steal) → wanted +1, Driving XP; you can then drive. Mission cars delivered to garage for cash.
- Heist finale: multi-step quest chain.
- Taxi job? Maybe enough.

Story quest chain "The Grove Street Score" with 6 stages, shown in quest log:
1. Talk to Lamar (Grove St) → steal a Ballas car (a marked purple car at Ballas turf) and drive it to the garage → reward cash.
2. Talk to Lester (hacker) at Vespucci → hack 2 ATMs (click ATMs with Hacking ≥?) → reward.
3. Talk to Franklin → eliminate 4 Ballas gangsters at the cul-de-sac → reward.
4. Talk to Trevor (Sandy Shores) → steal a truck? Maybe deliver 3 cars.
5. Heist: talk to Lester at bank, need pistol + 3 gang kills? Bank vault click → get $5000 but 3-star wanted.
6. Escape to Pay'n'Spray → complete.

Could simplify to 5 steps but still substantial. Also side jobs: 
- "Repair" broken cars (Mechanics XP + $50).
- "Deliver" pizza? Skip.
- Fishing/Cooking loop.
- Pickpocket pedestrians (Stealing XP + $).
- Rob 24/7 store (click counter with gun equipped → cash + 2 stars).
- Street races? Maybe too much.

Cars: implement simple arcade driving. Player enters car, WASD to drive, car has speed/heading, collisions with buildings slow it. Passengers? No. Shooting from car? Skip. Exit car with E. Cars have health; crashes damage; if 0 → explodes? mild.

Rendering:
- Isometric? No — top-down 2D with slight 3D-looking buildings (rect with height offset/shadow, roof details). OSRS is 3D-ish but 2D top-down is achievable and can look great.
- Ground: tiles with roads, sidewalks, grass, sand, water, park, plaza, parking lots. Draw roads with lane markings. Add details: streetlights, palms, hydrants, parked cars, trash, graffiti.
- Buildings: drawn as footprint with shadow + roof; some with sign text; entrances as doors. Buildings are solid tiles. Rendering order: ground, shadows, objects/cars/npcs/player sorted by y.
- Day/night cycle? Could be a nice touch: sky tint slowly changes, neon at night. Maybe allow time toggle? Keep static golden-hour/dusk vibe? A day-night cycle with lights is a big visual win. Implement time-of-day tint overlay and window lights at night, plus headlights on cars. Start at dusk. Cycle 8 min? Hmm, keep a toggle-able cycle maybe. Simpler: fixed sunset (golden) with long shadows — cinematic. Or cycle slowly and show clock in HUD. I'll do slow cycle ~10 min and start at 18:00 (dusk), with lights at night. Nice.
- Minimap: canvas in HUD corner, shows roads/buildings/player/cops/quest markers. Click to move? OSRS minimap is clickable; optional.
- HUD: top-left player card with combat level, HP bar, wanted stars, cash; top-right minimap + clock; bottom inventory panel (OSRS style) with tabs for skills/quests/map? RuneScape layout: inventory bottom right, skills bottom left, chatbox. For a game feel, do: left side vertical skills summary; bottom-right inventory grid; bottom-left contextual text/notifications.
